reason: While the text clearly portrays the Hebrews (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) as a distinct nation, it does not portray them as possessing their own specific land. The passage depicts them as enslaved in Egypt, laboring under Egyptian taskmasters to build Egyptian storage cities (Pithom and Raamses). The Hebrews are portrayed as a subject population within Egypt's territory, not as inhabitants of their own land. Although the broader Exodus narrative eventually involves a promised land, this fragment situates the Hebrew nation within Egyptian territory under foreign domination.
